title: Observables for cyclic causal set cosmologies
relevance: Sec. V Eq. (29) defines the posts observable algebra; Theorem 14-15 gives doubly-principal generators up to P_infty-complement; Eqs. (30)-(31) formulate a variation criterion and explicitly leave complex transitive-percolation extension inconclusive.
assumptions: Cyclic causal-set setting with infinitely many posts; extension criterion applied to the doubly-reduced tree and prescribed complex transitive-percolation amplitudes.
conclusion: The authors state that their doubly-reduced complex-percolation extension test is inconclusive and identify future computation of a post-related variation sum as relevant.
proof_status: Relevant sections read in full-text HTML; no proof of the rank-only all-principal post-value classification located in these sections.
dependencies: The paper adapts the bounded-variation criteria of its cited complex sequential growth literature.
limits: Does not impose the audited rule nu(D_H)=kappa_n N(H)A_p(H) for every principal H. Version/date metadata are unusual because v2 HTML displays a 2026 date despite v2 arXiv timestamp 2023-07-17.
open_questions: Could later work settle the doubly-reduced or rank-only post-value extension question?

title: A Criterion for Covariance in Complex Sequential Growth Models
relevance: Sec. 3.1 Theorem 3.1 and Claims 3.2-3.3 give bounded-variation and extension criteria for complex sequential-growth cylinder measures; the algebraic method is a predecessor to the total-variation argument.
assumptions: Complex sequential growth with scalar or finite-dimensional vector-valued amplitudes on the full generated event sigma-algebra; finite-level cylinders partition the labeled history space.
conclusion: Summability of maximal level variation excess suffices for bounded variation; divergence of minimal excess obstructs bounded variation. The paper constructs examples and treats complex percolation as a known nonextension case.
proof_status: Relevant full-text sections read; proof detail checked at theorem and level-sum argument.
dependencies: Cites the earlier Dowker-Johnston-Surya complex percolation analysis and vector measure theory.
limits: Not the covariant posts algebra with an independently specified rank-dependent post factor; no matching theorem found in the examined sections.
locator: Sec. 3.1, Theorem 3.1, Claims 3.2-3.3; Sec. 3.3 complex-percolation discussion
open_questions: Does any later application transfer these full-algebra criteria to shape-blind post values on the covariant posts algebra?

title: On extending the Quantum Measure
relevance: Sec. 4 treats complex percolation and its extension to the full labelled history sigma-algebra; closest nonextension predecessor.
assumptions: Complex percolation with p+q=1 and prescribed finite cylinder amplitudes on the labeled event algebra; scalar case is the one-dimensional vector-measure case.
conclusion: The scalar complex-percolation premeasure does not extend to a bounded-variation measure on the full labeled sigma-algebra except when p and q are both real and nonnegative; with p+q=1 this is p in [0,1].
proof_status: Full-text Sec. 4 read; argument uses variation of labeled level partitions.
dependencies: Uses the vector-measure framework developed earlier in the same paper.
limits: Full labeled algebra is larger than the posts algebra; it does not state the rank-only post-value rule or settle whether that smaller covariant problem admits such measures.
open_questions: Is there a theorem showing this full labelled sigma-algebra obstruction transfers to the smaller posts algebra under additional post-value constraints?

title: The Structure of Random Graph Orders
relevance: Finite random-graph-order post occurrence and decomposition into linear sums when there are many posts; structural predecessor for posts and ordinal decompositions.
assumptions: Finite random graph order P_{n,p}, with independent forward edges and transitive closure; asymptotic conditions on p and n for post occurrence.
conclusion: Abstract states an asymptotic criterion for existence/nonexistence of posts and uses post-induced linear-sum decomposition to study random-order statistics.
proof_status: Discovery/abstract only; exact theorem proof not read in this lane.
limits: Not a complex measure result or a rank-factor classification; finite asymptotics differ from the one-way infinite classical post-tail statement.
version: SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 10 (1997), DOI 10.1137/S0895480194281215

title: A Computation of the Expected Number of Posts in a Finite Random Graph Order
relevance: Sec. 2, Theorem 2.1 and Eqs. (1)-(2) give one-way infinite random graph order post probabilities via Euler-product factors; reports Alon et al.'s earlier infinite-post theorem.
assumptions: Independent forward edges with real probability 0<p<1 and transitive closure on a one-way infinite random graph order; finite-order expectation analysis also included.
conclusion: For N-order random graph, post probability involves finite/limiting Euler products; paper states infinite many posts almost surely was first proved by Alon et al., with proof adaptation to N described as straightforward.
proof_status: Full-text relevant section read; the cited Alon et al. original proof not independently obtained or reproduced.
dependencies: Cites Alon et al. for almost-sure infinite posts on Z.
limits: Classical probability only. Supports positive-real sufficiency as prior input, not the complex no-go or factorization axiom.
open_questions: What is the exact original Alon et al. theorem and proof for infinitely many posts on the two-way infinite order?

title: Linear extensions of a random partial order
relevance: Bombelli-Seggev-Watson identify this as the source proving the mean post count in the two-way infinite random graph order; likely primary predecessor for infinite posts.
assumptions: Random partial order / random graph order; exact posts statement is not extracted here.
conclusion: Discovery only; not used as a verified proof source in this audit.

dependencies: Identified through the BSW paper's reference and search result.
